key_concepts: Free-fall occurs when gravity is the only force and air resistance is absent
Acceleration due to gravity is 9.8 m/s/s downward, symbolized g, and is negative
Free-fall speed changes by 9.8 m/s every second
Aristotle's theory was qualitative and held that heavy objects fall faster than lighter on
Galileo tested motion experimentally and showed all objects fall at the same rate without
Galileo found d/t² is constant and equals acceleration due to gravity
An object thrown upward slows by 9.8 m/s each second and has positive velocity
A dropped object speeds up by 9.8 m/s each second and has negative velocity
Displacement in free-fall increases with time and is computed using d = ½ gt²
At maximum height, an object's speed is momentarily zero
An object thrown upward returns to its starting height with equal speed but opposite direc
Reaction time can be calculated from a falling ruler using d = ½ gt²
